subject: Science
question: What is a naturally occurring magnetic rock/mineral consisting of iron oxide (Fe₃O₄) that was discovered in ancient Greece?
explanation: Magnetite is a natural permanent magnet discovered in Magnesia, ancient Greece, also called 'lodestone' ('leading stone').

subject: Science
question: Who was the ancient Greek shepherd who discovered natural magnetic rock when the iron tip of his walking stick and iron nails in his shoes got stuck to a black rock?
explanation: Legend says the shepherd Magnes discovered magnetic ore on Mount Ida when his iron-tipped staff stuck to magnetite rocks.

subject: Science
question: Materials that are attracted strongly towards a magnet (such as iron, nickel, cobalt, and steel) are called:
explanation: Ferromagnetic materials containing unpaired d-electrons (Fe, Ni, Co) are attracted to magnetic fields.

subject: Science
question: Materials that are NOT attracted towards a magnet (such as wood, plastic, rubber, glass, paper, gold, aluminium) are called:
explanation: Non-magnetic materials lack permanent atomic magnetic dipoles and do not exhibit magnetic attraction.

subject: Science
question: How many magnetic poles does EVERY magnet possess, regardless of its shape or size?
options: Two poles (North Pole 'N' and South Pole 'S')
explanation: Magnetic dipoles always exist in pairs: a North-seeking pole (N) and a South-seeking pole (S).

subject: Science
question: Where is the magnetic force (attraction power) of a bar magnet the STRONGEST?
options: Near its two end Poles (North and South Poles)
Exactly at the center of the magnet
explanation: Magnetic field flux density converges at the two terminal poles, where iron filings cling in dense clusters.

subject: Science
question: In which geographical direction does a freely suspended bar magnet ALWAYS come to rest?
explanation: A freely pivoted magnet aligns with Earth's geomagnetic field lines along the geographic North-South meridian.

subject: Science
question: What navigational instrument uses a magnetized needle freely pivoted inside a dial to find geographical directions?
explanation: A magnetic compass features a pivoted magnetized needle whose painted North tip indicates geomagnetic north.

subject: Science
question: What happens when two LIKE magnetic poles (North and North, or South and South) are brought close to each other?
options: They REPEL (push away from) each other
explanation: Fundamental magnetic law: Like poles repel (N-N or S-S); unlike poles attract (N-S).

subject: Science
question: What happens when two UNLIKE magnetic poles (North and South) are brought close to each other?
explanation: Opposite magnetic polarities (N and S) experience mutual attractive Lorentz/dipolar forces.

subject: Science
question: Which of the following is a classic artificial shape of manufactured permanent magnets?
options: Bar magnet, Horse-shoe magnet, Cylindrical magnet, and Ball-ended magnet
explanation: Artificial magnets are cast/sintered in bar, horseshoe, disc, cylindrical, and ring geometries.

subject: Science
question: What is the surest and only foolproof test to confirm whether an unknown metal piece is an active magnet or merely a magnetic iron piece?
options: REPULSION test (only another magnet will experience repulsion; an ordinary iron piece is attracted to both poles)
explanation: Unmagnetized ferromagnetic iron is attracted by both N and S poles; only a true magnet repels like poles.

subject: Science
question: What happens when a bar magnet is cut or broken into TWO halves across its middle?
options: Each broken piece becomes a complete, independent magnet with its own North and South Pole (Magnetic monopoles do NOT exist)
One piece becomes pure North pole and the other pure South pole
Both pieces lose all magnetism permanently
explanation: Atomic magnetic domains remain dipolar; cutting a magnet creates two smaller dipoles each with N and S poles.

subject: Science
question: How can you magnetize an ordinary iron nail or sewing needle using the 'Single-Touch' method?
options: Stroke the iron nail with one pole of a bar magnet repeatedly in ONE fixed direction along its length (30–40 times) without reversing direction
Rub the magnet back and forth randomly
Heat the nail in a fire with the magnet
Drop the nail in cold water
explanation: Unidirectional stroking aligns magnetic Weiss domains in the ferromagnetic nail along the stroke vector.

subject: Science
question: Which of the following actions can cause a permanent magnet to LOSE its magnetism (Demagnetization)?
options: Heating to high temperatures, hammering vigorously with a mallet, or dropping it repeatedly from a height onto hard floor
Keeping it in a dark wooden box
Using it to pick up paper clips
explanation: Thermal energy (above Curie temperature) and mechanical impact randomize aligned magnetic domain orientations.

subject: Science
question: How should Bar Magnets be safely stored in pairs to preserve their magnetic strength over years?
options: Stored in pairs with UNLIKE poles opposite each other, separated by a wooden spacer in the middle and connected by soft iron pieces (Keepers) across their ends
Stored loose in an iron bucket
explanation: Soft iron magnetic keepers close magnetic flux loops, preventing self-demagnetizing free pole dissipation.

subject: Science
question: How should a Horseshoe Magnet be stored properly?
options: By placing a single piece of soft iron (magnetic keeper) across its two open poles
By wrapping it in aluminium foil
explanation: A soft iron keeper across both adjacent poles of a horseshoe magnet bridges the gap, completing the magnetic circuit.

subject: Science
question: Why does the Earth itself behave like a colossal gigantic magnet?
options: Circulating molten iron-nickel liquid currents in Earth's outer core generate a geomagnetic field, with its magnetic south pole located near the geographic North Pole
Because Earth is made of giant plastic magnets
explanation: Geodynamo convection in the outer core generates Earth's geomagnetic field; geographic North hosts geomagnetic South polarity.

subject: Science
question: What ancient Chinese legend describes an emperor's chariot equipped with a rotating wooden statue holding an outstretched arm that always pointed SOUTH?
options: The South-Pointing Chariot of Emperor Huang Di
explanation: Huang Di's legendary chariot utilized a lodestone/geared mechanism whose statue arm consistently pointed South.

subject: Science
question: Why should permanent strong magnets be kept away from cassette tapes, credit cards, computer hard drives, and mobile phones?
options: The strong magnetic field can alter or erase the magnetic data encoded on magnetic strips, chips, and micro-circuitry
Because magnets will catch fire near phones
Because phones will become too heavy
Because phone glass turns into mirror
explanation: External stray magnetic flux can corrupt magnetically stored binary bits and saturate Hall sensors in electronics.

subject: Science
question: If an iron needle is magnetized by stroking with the North pole of a bar magnet starting from end A to end B, what magnetic pole is formed at end B?
options: South Pole (opposite to the stroking pole)
explanation: The trailing end B of the stroke acquires opposite polarity (South pole) to the departing North pole.

subject: Science
question: Can magnetic force act through non-magnetic barriers (like a sheet of paper, cardboard, or a plastic ruler)?
options: Yes, magnetic field lines penetrate through non-magnetic materials like paper, glass, plastic, and water effortlessly
No, paper blocks all magnetic forces completely
Only if the paper is wet
explanation: Magnetic flux permeates non-ferromagnetic dielectric media with magnetic permeability μ ≈ μ₀.

subject: Science
question: A tailor dropped a box of sewing needles into a box of sawdust. What is the fastest and easiest way to separate all the steel needles without searching by hand?
options: Pass a strong magnet through the sawdust; all steel needles will cling to the magnet instantly
explanation: Magnetic separation extracts ferromagnetic steel needles while leaving non-magnetic sawdust behind.

subject: Science
question: Which of the following modern technological devices utilizes powerful magnets to operate?
options: Electric motors, Dynamos, MRI medical scanners, Maglev trains, and Audio speakers
explanation: Electromagnetic induction and magnetic levitation power electric motors, Maglev transit, MRI tomography, and acoustic transducers.

subject: Science
question: How does a Maglev (Magnetic Levitation) high-speed bullet train run without touching the track rails?
options: Superconducting electromagnets on the train and track repel each other with strong like magnetic poles, levitating the train in air and eliminating mechanical friction
It rolls on millions of tiny ball bearings
It floats on a layer of hot steam
explanation: Electrodynamic/electromagnetic levitation utilizes magnetic repulsion to float carriages ~10–15 mm above guideways.

subject: Science
question: What is an 'Electromagnet'?
options: A temporary magnet formed by winding an insulated copper wire around a soft iron core and passing electric current through it
A rock found in the ocean
A permanent bar magnet that never loses magnetism
A magnet made of pure plastic
explanation: An electromagnet generates a controllable magnetic field via current flow through an insulated solenoid coil.

subject: Science
question: Why do iron filings sprinkle on a sheet of paper over a bar magnet arrange themselves in distinct curved lines?
options: Each tiny iron filing becomes a miniature induced magnet and aligns along the invisible curved Magnetic Field Lines running from North to South pole
Because of gravity pulling them sideways
explanation: Induced magnetic dipolar moments torque iron filings tangent to lines of magnetic flux density.

subject: Science
question: What happens if a freely suspended bar magnet is brought near another strong magnet?
options: The suspended magnet will rotate and re-align: its North pole will be attracted to the other's South pole and repelled by its North pole
It will ignore the second magnet
explanation: Torque τ = m × B causes the pivoted dipole to rotate until its magnetic moment aligns with the external field.

subject: Science
question:
Read the statements:
Assertion (A): It is physically impossible to isolate a single, independent magnetic monopole (pure North or pure South pole) in classical physics.
Reason (R): Magnetism originates from circulating microscopic atomic electron dipoles; breaking a magnet simply divides the dipoles, creating pairs of North and South poles in every fragment.
Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).
explanation: Gauss's Law for Magnetism (∇ · B = 0) establishes that magnetic field lines are continuous closed loops without monopole sources.

subject: Science

options: The bar is a magnet; end X is a North Pole and end Y is a South Pole
The bar is ordinary non-magnetic aluminium
End X is a South Pole
The bar is unmagnetized soft iron
explanation: Repulsion definitively confirms that bar X-Y is a magnet and end X is a North pole.

subject: Science
question: Why does the geographic North Pole of Earth attract the NORTH-seeking pole of a compass needle?
options: Because Earth's geomagnetic SOUTH magnetic pole is physically located near the geographic North Pole, exerting attractive force on the needle's North pole
Because like poles attract in space
Because geographic north has positive electricity
Because the compass is upside down
explanation: Earth's internal magnetic dipole is inverted relative to geography: the geomagnetic South pole resides near Arctic geographic North.

subject: Science
question: A heavy-duty industrial magnetic crane in a junkyard lifts 5 tonnes of scrap iron cars and drops them precisely into a furnace. How does the crane operator release the scrap iron instantly?

By hitting the magnet with a hammer
By spraying cold water on the cars
By turning the crane upside down
explanation: Electromagnets provide instantaneous on/off control: cutting the solenoid circuit demagnetizes the soft iron core, dropping the load.

question:

All rings stick tightly without gaps

subject: Science
question: Why is Soft Iron preferred over Hard Steel for making magnetic keepers and cores of electromagnets?
options: Soft iron has high magnetic permeability and low retentivity, magnetizing and demagnetizing instantly without retaining permanent residual magnetism
Because soft iron is cheaper than wood

He walked across the ocean on foot
explanation: Fa Xian's travelogue chronicles the terror of monsoonal typhoons, clinging to his precious Buddhist manuscripts on board.

subject: Social Science
question: What strict entrance examination did students have to pass to gain admission into Nalanda University, according to Xuan Zang?
options: The Gatekeeper (Dvarapandita) posed deep philosophical questions at the main entrance gate; only 20% to 30% of applicants could answer and gain admission
They had to pay 100 gold coins
They had to run a 5-mile race
They had to belong to royal families
explanation: Xuan Zang noted that Nalanda maintained rigorous academic standards, screening applicants through oral philosophical disputation.

subject: Social Science
question: Who was the South Indian Bhakti poet-saint Appar (a devotee of Lord Shiva) who composed soulful devotional poems in Tamil celebrating equality?
options: A 7th-century Nayanar saint who was a Vellalar (farmer)
explanation: Appar (Thirunavukkarasar), a peasant Vellalar, composed Tevaram hymns proclaiming that sincere devotion supersedes caste origins.

subject: Social Science
question: What three ruling dynasties were known as the 'Muvendar' (Three Crowned Kings) who controlled the fertile Kaveri delta and southern coastal ports around 2,300 years ago?
options: The Cholas, the Cheras, and the Pandyas
explanation: Sangam literature celebrates the 'Muvendar': the Cholas (Uraiyur/Puhar), Cheras (Karur/Muziris), and Pandyas (Madurai/Korkai).

subject: Social Science
question: What was Puhar (also known as Kaveripattinam) in ancient South India?
options: The premier coastal port city of the early Cholas on the Bay of Bengal, bustling with international sea trade
explanation: Puhar was the bustling maritime port of the Cholas, vividly depicted in the Tamil epic 'Silappadikaram'.

subject: Social Science
question: What Indian commodity was so prized in the ancient Roman Empire that it was popularly called 'Black Gold' (Yavanapriya)?
explanation: Malabar black pepper was in such huge demand in Rome that it was traded for its weight in gold and termed 'Black Gold'.

subject: Social Science
question: How did ancient sailors and merchant navigators cross the Arabian Sea to reach the western ports of India quickly?
options: They took strategic advantage of the seasonal Southwest Monsoon winds to sail directly across the open ocean from the Gulf of Aden to the Malabar coast in summer
By rowing continuously by hand without sails
By following stars in winter only
explanation: Hippalus and Greek sailors harnessed the predictable seasonal Southwest Monsoon winds to sail straight across the open Arabian Sea.

subject: Social Science
question: What is the primary spiritual concept behind the construction of magnificent Hindu temple architecture that evolved from the Bhakti movement?
options: Creating sacred physical abodes (Prasad/Garbhagriha) where the chosen deity resides to receive personal loving worship and darshan from devotees
explanation: Bhakti catalyzed temple architecture: housing the enshrined deity in the sanctum sanctorum (Garbhagriha) for direct darshan.

subject: Social Science
question:
Read the statements:
Assertion (A): The expansion of the Silk Route was as much an intellectual and cultural highway as it was an international commercial highway.
Reason (R): Along with silk, glassware, and spices, the route carried Buddhist philosophy, monastic texts, art styles (Gandhara-Mathura), and religious pilgrims between India, Central Asia, and East Asia.
Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).
explanation: Trade routes operated as cultural transmission vectors, diffusing Buddhism, art, technology (paper/silk), and languages across Eurasia.

subject: Social Science
question:
Spot the IMPOSTER in the following group of ancient Chinese pilgrims who visited India to study Buddhist texts:
Group: [Fa Xian (Faxian), Xuan Zang (Hiuen Tsang), I-Qing (Yijing), Megasthenes]
explanation: Megasthenes was a GREEK ambassador from Seleucus Nicator to Chandragupta Maurya (author of 'Indica'), NOT a Chinese Buddhist pilgrim.

subject: Social Science
question:
Consider the theological evolution between Early Buddhism (Theravada) and Later Buddhism (Mahayana):
Which of the following is a definitive characteristic of MAHAYANA Buddhism?
options: Depicting Buddha in anthropomorphic human statue form and worshipping Bodhisattvas who postpone nirvana to save all sentient beings
Strictly representing Buddha through aniconic symbols (footprints, empty throne, wheel)
Using only Pali language and rejecting Sanskrit
explanation: Mahayana transitioned from aniconism to iconographic idol worship, adopting Sanskrit and the Bodhisattva ideal.

subject: Social Science
question:
Match Column I (Ancient Personalities / Texts) with Column II (Historical Contributions):
(a) Kanishka     -> (i) Author of Buddhacharita in Sanskrit
(b) Ashvaghosha  -> (ii) Kushana Emperor who convened 4th Buddhist Council
(c) Xuan Zang    -> (iii) Pilgrim who spent 16 years studying at Nalanda
(d) Appar        -> (iv) Nayanar saint who composed Tamil devotional hymns
explanation: Kanishka = 4th Council; Ashvaghosha = Buddhacharita; Xuan Zang = Nalanda scholar; Appar = Nayanar saint.

subject: Social Science
question:
Read the statements regarding ancient pilgrims:
Statement 1: Xuan Zang lost 50 precious manuscripts in the Indus river when his boat capsized during his return journey.
Statement 2: Nalanda University charged high tuition fees in gold from all students.
Statement 3: Roman coins have been discovered in large hoards across South India.
Which statements are TRUE?
explanation: Statement 2 is false because education, lodging, and food at Nalanda were completely free, funded by revenue from 100 endowed villages. Statements 1 and 3 are true.

subject: Social Science
question: What was the administrative concept of 'Muvendar' mentioned in Sangam poems, where each of the three ruling chiefs had TWO centers of power?
options: Each dynasty (Cholas, Cheras, Pandyas) maintained ONE inland capital city and ONE coastal seaport, totaling six major urban power hubs in South India
Each had two kings ruling at once
Each ruled over two separate islands
explanation: Dual nodes of power: Cholas (Uraiyur inland + Puhar port), Pandyas (Madurai inland + Korkai port), Cheras (Karur inland + Muziris port).

subject: Social Science
question: Why did the Kushana rulers issue such high-denomination, pure GOLD coins around the 1st century CE?
options: To facilitate large-scale international transactions on the Silk Route, fueled by massive inflows of Roman gold and overland transit profits
Because they had no copper or silver
To give as gifts to pilgrims
To melt and build gold palaces
explanation: Kushana gold dinars mirrored Roman imperial weight standards (8 grams), creating a convertible reserve currency along the Silk Road.

subject: Social Science
question:
Consider four events in the history of trade and pilgrimage:
1. Invention of silk making in China (c. 5000 BCE)
2. Reign of Kanishka and Mahayana Buddhism (c. 78 CE)
3. Visit of Chinese pilgrim Fa Xian (c. 400 CE)
4. Visit of Chinese pilgrim Xuan Zang (c. 630 CE)
Arrange them in chronological order from OLDEST to MOST RECENT:
explanation: Silk invention (5000 BCE) > Kanishka (78 CE) > Fa Xian (400 CE) > Xuan Zang (630 CE).

subject: Social Science
question: What role did Buddhist monastic establishments along trade routes (such as Kanheri, Karle, and Ajanta rock-cut chaityas and viharas) play in ancient commerce?
options: They served as secure rest stops, financial banking vaults, and provisioning stations for traveling merchant caravans passing through Western Ghat passes
explanation: Rock-cut viharas located along mountain passes (Bhor Ghat, Thal Ghat) offered safe lodging, credit, and water for merchant guilds.

subject: Social Science
question: How did the Bhakti philosophy transform Indian art, poetry, and regional vernacular languages?
options: It inspired an explosion of devotional poetry, music, and sculpture composed in popular regional spoken languages (Tamil, Kannada, Marathi, Hindi) rather than exclusive elite Sanskrit alone
It mandated writing books only in Greek
explanation: Bhakti democratized culture, spawning vernacular literature (Tevaram, Divya Prabandham) and emotive temple sculpture.

subject: Social Science
question: What is the profound philosophical meaning behind the Bhagavad Gita's teaching on 'Nishkama Karma' in the context of Bhakti?
options: Performing one's righteous duty selflessly without selfish attachment to the fruits or rewards of action, dedicating all outcomes in love to the Divine
Renouncing all work and sitting idle
Fighting wars to acquire personal wealth
Doing good deeds only for praise
explanation: Nishkama Karma unites selfless duty with spiritual devotion, purifying human intent of egoistic desire.

subject: Social Science
question: What grand historical synthesis does Chapter 10 of NCERT History reveal about the ancient world?
options: A dynamic, interconnected world where trans-continental trade corridors, imperial patronage, philosophical reformations, and spiritual pilgrimages fostered deep cross-cultural synthesis across human civilization
A collection of completely isolated civilizations with zero contact
A world where only war existed without trade
A primitive society without roads or ideas
explanation: The chapter portrays an open, interconnected global ancient world enriched by trade, intellectual cross-pollination, and shared spiritual quest.

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: जिस शब्द से किसी कार्य के करने या होने का बोध होता है (जैसे: पढ़ना, लिखना, दौड़ना, खाना, सोना, होना), उसे व्याकरण में क्या कहते हैं?
explanation: कार्य के निष्पादन या स्वतः होने का बोध कराने वाले विकारी शब्द 'क्रिया' कहलाते हैं।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: क्रिया के मूल रूप (Basic root form) को क्या कहते हैं, जिससे विभिन्न क्रिया पद बनते हैं (जैसे: 'पढ़' से पढ़ना, पढ़ता, पढ़ेगा)?
explanation: क्रिया के मूल अविभाज्य रूप को 'धातु' कहते हैं (जैसे: लिख, खा, देख, गा, हँस)। धातु में 'ना' प्रत्यय जोड़कर सामान्य क्रिया बनती है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: कर्म के आधार पर क्रिया के मुख्य रूप से कितने भेद होते हैं?
options: दो भेद (1. सकर्मक क्रिया, और 2. अकर्मक क्रिया)
explanation: कर्म की अपेक्षा के आधार पर क्रिया के 2 प्रमुख भेद हैं: सकर्मक (कर्म सहित) और अकर्मक (कर्म रहित)।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: जिस क्रिया के व्यापार (कार्य) का फल कर्ता पर न पड़कर 'कर्म' पर पड़ता है (अर्थात् जिसमें कर्म की आवश्यकता होती है), उसे क्या कहते हैं?
options: सकर्मक क्रिया (Transitive Verb - जैसे: 'राम पुस्तक पढ़ता है')
explanation: जिस क्रिया का प्रभाव कर्म पर पड़े (क्या/किसे का उत्तर मिले), वह 'सकर्मक क्रिया' होती है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: जिस क्रिया के व्यापार का फल सीधे कर्ता पर ही पड़ता है और जिसमें कर्म नहीं होता (जैसे: 'बच्चा रोता है', 'पक्षी उड़ते हैं'), उसे क्या कहते हैं?
explanation: जिसमें कर्म की अपेक्षा न हो और कार्य का प्रभाव कर्ता पर ही सीमित रहे, वह 'अकर्मक क्रिया' होती है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: वाक्य में क्रिया के साथ 'क्या' या 'किसे/किसको' लगाकर प्रश्न पूछने पर यदि कोई उत्तर मिलता है, तो वह क्रिया क्या कहलाती है?
options: सकर्मक क्रिया (उत्तर मिलने वाला पद 'कर्म' होता है)
explanation: 'क्या/किसे' प्रश्न का सार्थक उत्तर मिलना सकर्मक क्रिया की सबसे सरल व प्रामाणिक पहचान है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: जिस सकर्मक क्रिया में दो कर्म होते हैं (जैसे: 'अध्यापक ने छात्रों को हिंदी पढ़ाई'), उसे क्या कहते हैं?
options: द्विकर्मक क्रिया (छात्रों = गौण कर्म ; हिंदी = मुख्य कर्म)
explanation: दो कर्मों (मुख्य कर्म वस्तुवाचक + गौण कर्म प्राणीवाचक) से युक्त क्रिया 'द्विकर्मक क्रिया' कहलाती है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: जब कर्ता स्वयं कार्य न करके किसी अन्य को कार्य करने की प्रेरणा देता है या करवाता है (जैसे: 'माँ नौकरानी से कपड़े धुलवाती है'), तो उस क्रिया को क्या कहते हैं?
explanation: कर्ता द्वारा किसी अन्य को कार्य में प्रवृत्त कराने वाली क्रिया 'प्रेरणार्थक क्रिया' कहलाती है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: संज्ञा, सर्वनाम या विशेषण शब्दों से बनने वाली क्रियाओं (जैसे: 'हाथ' से हथियाना, 'बात' से बतियाना, 'शर्म' से शर्माना, 'गर्म' से गरमाना) को क्या कहते हैं?
explanation: संज्ञा/सर्वनाम/विशेषण प्रातिपदिकों में प्रत्यय जोड़कर निर्मित क्रियाएँ 'नामधातु क्रिया' कहलाती हैं।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: जब दो या दो से अधिक क्रियाएँ मिलकर एक पूर्ण क्रिया बनाती हैं (जैसे: 'वह खाना **खा चुका है**', 'मोहन **चला गया**'), तो उन्हें क्या कहते हैं?
explanation: मुख्य क्रिया और रंजक क्रिया के संयोग से गठित क्रिया पद 'संयुक्त क्रिया' कहलाते हैं।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: मुख्य क्रिया से पहले होने वाली क्रिया (जिसमें प्रायः 'कर' या 'करके' लगा होता है, जैसे: 'वह **नहाकर** विद्यालय गया') को क्या कहते हैं?
explanation: समापिका क्रिया से पूर्व निष्पादित क्रिया 'पूर्वकालिक क्रिया' कहलाती है (जैसे: पढ़कर, खेलकर, खाकर)।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: मुख्य क्रिया के साथ जुड़कर काल और अर्थ को स्पष्ट करने वाली क्रिया (जैसे: 'है', 'था', 'रहा है', 'होगा') को क्या कहते हैं?
explanation: काल और पक्ष की सिद्धि में मुख्य क्रिया की सहायता करने वाले पद 'सहायक क्रिया' कहलाते हैं।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question:
वाक्य में प्रयुक्त क्रिया का सही भेद पहचानिए:
'रोहन मैदान में पतंग **उड़ा रहा है**।'
explanation: प्रश्न: 'क्या उड़ा रहा है?' -> उत्तर: 'पतंग' (कर्म उपस्थित है, अतः सकर्मक क्रिया है)।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question:
वाक्य में प्रयुक्त क्रिया का सही भेद पहचानिए:
'आकाश में पक्षी **उड़ रहे हैं**।'
options: अकर्मक क्रिया (उड़ने का फल कर्ता 'पक्षी' पर है, कोई कर्म नहीं है)
explanation: यहाँ 'आकाश में' अधिकरण कारक (स्थान) है, कर्म नहीं; उड़ने का व्यापार कर्ता में घटित हो रहा है, अतः अकर्मक क्रिया है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: निम्नलिखित में से स्वाभाविक रूप से 'अकर्मक क्रियाओं' का सही समूह कौन-सा है?
options: हँसना, रोना, सोना, जागना, उड़ना, तैरना, बैठना, चलना
पढ़ना, लिखना, खाना, पीना, देखना, बनाना
explanation: शारीरिक स्थितियाँ एवं स्वाभाविक गतियाँ (हँसना, रोना, सोना, दौड़ना) स्वतः अकर्मक क्रियाएँ होती हैं।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: प्रेरणार्थक क्रिया के दो रूप (प्रथम प्रेरणार्थक और द्वितीय प्रेरणार्थक) का सही उदाहरण कौन-सा है?
options: मूल: पढ़ना -> प्रथम: पढ़ाना -> द्वितीय: पढ़वाना
मूल: खाना -> प्रथम: खाया -> द्वितीय: खाएगा
मूल: चलना -> प्रथम: चला -> द्वितीय: चल
मूल: लिखना -> प्रथम: लिखा -> द्वितीय: लेख
explanation: प्रथम प्रेरणार्थक में '-आना' (पढ़ाना) तथा द्वितीय प्रेरणार्थक में '-वाना' (पढ़वाना) प्रत्यय जुड़ता है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question:
वाक्य में प्रयुक्त दोनों कर्मों की सही पहचान कीजिए:
'पिता जी ने **पुत्र को** **घड़ी** दी।'
options: घड़ी = मुख्य कर्म (प्रत्यक्ष/निर्जीव) ; पुत्र = गौण कर्म (अप्रत्यक्ष/सजीव)
घड़ी = गौण कर्म ; पुत्र = मुख्य कर्म
explanation: 'क्या दिया?' -> घड़ी (मुख्य कर्म); 'किसे दिया?' -> पुत्र को (गौण कर्म)।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: संज्ञा शब्द 'लाठी' और 'फिल्म' से बनने वाली सही नामधातु क्रियाएँ क्रमशः क्या हैं?
explanation: लाठी -> लठियाना; फिल्म -> फिल्माना (नामधातु क्रियाएँ)।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: विशेषण शब्द 'चिकना' और 'अपना' (सर्वनाम) से बनने वाली सही नामधातु क्रियाएँ क्या हैं?
explanation: चिकना (विशेषण) -> चिकनाना; अपना (सर्वनाम) -> अपनाना।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question:
वाक्य में प्रयुक्त रेखांकित पद का क्रिया भेद बताइए:
'वह पत्र **लिखवाता है**।'
options: प्रेरणार्थक क्रिया (कर्ता स्वयं न लिखकर किसी दूसरे से लिखवाता है)
explanation: 'लिखवाना' द्वितीय प्रेरणार्थक क्रिया है, जिसमें कर्ता प्रेरक बनकर अन्य से कार्य संपन्न कराता है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question:
वाक्य में प्रयुक्त रेखांकित पद का क्रिया भेद बताइए:
'छात्र पुस्तक **पढ़कर** सो गया।'
options: पूर्वकालिक क्रिया ('पढ़कर' सोने की मुख्य क्रिया से पूर्व संपन्न हुई है)
explanation: सोने से पूर्व 'पढ़ना' क्रिया पूर्ण हुई है, अतः 'पढ़कर' पूर्वकालिक क्रिया है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: संयुक्त क्रिया 'रोहन खेलने लगा' में मुख्य क्रिया और रंजक (सहायक) क्रिया कौन-सी है?
explanation: 'खेलने' मुख्य अर्थ दे रहा है, और 'लगा' क्रिया के आरंभ होने का रंजक अर्थ जोड़ रहा है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: वाक्य में प्रयुक्त क्रिया का लिंग और वचन किसके अनुसार निर्धारित होता है?
options: सामान्यतः कर्ता के लिंग-वचन के अनुसार ; किन्तु कर्मवाच्य में अथवा कर्ता के साथ 'ने' परसर्ग होने पर कर्म के लिंग-वचन के अनुसार
क्रिया का कोई लिंग-वचन नहीं होता
explanation: कर्तृप्रयोग में क्रिया कर्ता के अनुसार और कर्मणिप्रयोग (जैसे 'राम ने रोटी खाई') में कर्म के अनुसार प्रयुक्त होती है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question:
वाक्य में क्रिया का सही प्रयोग पहचानिए:
'सुधा ने एक मधुर गीत _______।'
options: गाया (कर्म 'गीत' पुल्लिंग एकवचन है, अतः क्रिया 'गाया' होगी)
explanation: 'ने' परसर्ग होने पर भूतकाल में क्रिया कर्म ('गीत' - पुल्लिंग एकवचन) के अनुसार 'गाया' होगी।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: अनुकरणात्मक धातुओं (ध्वनियों के अनुकरण से बनने वाली क्रियाएँ) का सही उदाहरण कौन-सा है?
explanation: ध्वनि के अनुकरण पर गढ़ी गई धातुएँ अनुकरणात्मक नामधातु क्रियाएँ कहलाती हैं (खटखट -> खटखटाना)।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question:
वाक्य में प्रयुक्त रेखांकित पद का क्रिया भेद बताइए:
'माली पौधों को पानी **दे रहा है**।'
explanation: 'क्या दे रहा है?' -> पानी (कर्म उपस्थित है, अतः सकर्मक क्रिया है)।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: मूल धातु 'हँसना' का प्रथम और द्वितीय प्रेरणार्थक रूप क्या होगा?
explanation: हँसना -> हँसाना -> हँसवाना।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question:
वाक्य में प्रयुक्त रेखांकित पद का क्रिया भेद बताइए:
'शाम होते ही सूरज **डूब गया**।'
explanation: डूबने का फल कर्ता 'सूरज' पर है और यह 'डूबना' + 'गया' दो धातुओं से मिलकर बनी अकर्मक संयुक्त क्रिया है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question:
कथन और कारण को ध्यानपूर्वक पढ़ें:
कथन (A): 'बच्चा रात भर रोता रहा' वाक्य में 'रोता रहा' अकर्मक क्रिया है, भले ही वाक्य में 'रात भर' शब्द आया हो।
कारण (R): 'रात भर' कालवाचक क्रियाविशेषण (समय का द्योतक) है, कर्म नहीं; रोने की क्रिया का फल केवल कर्ता (बच्चा) पर पड़ता है।
सही विकल्प चुनें:
options: (A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं तथा (R), (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
(A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु (R), (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता।
explanation: काल/स्थान सूचक पद क्रियाविशेषण होते हैं, कर्म नहीं; अतः स्वाभाविक अकर्मक क्रिया अकर्मक ही रहती है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question:
Spot the IMPOSTER in the following group of क्रिया और उनके भेदों के युग्म में:
Group: [पढ़ना - सकर्मक, हँसना - अकर्मक, लिखना - सकर्मक, सोना - सकर्मक]
explanation: 'सोना - सकर्मक' अशुद्ध युग्म है; 'सोना' स्वाभाविक अकर्मक क्रिया (Intransitive Verb) है, सकर्मक नहीं।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question:
सुमेलित कीजिए (क्रिया के रूप और उनके व्याकरणिक भेद):
(क) हथियाना   -> (i) पूर्वकालिक क्रिया
(ख) पिलवाना    -> (ii) नामधातु क्रिया
(ग) खाकर      -> (iii) संयुक्त क्रिया
(घ) चल पड़ा   -> (iv) द्वितीय प्रेरणार्थक क्रिया
explanation: हथियाना = नामधातु; पिलवाना = द्वितीय प्रेरणार्थक; खाकर = पूर्वकालिक; चल पड़ा = संयुक्त क्रिया।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: सजातीय क्रिया (Cognate Verb) का सही उदाहरण कौन-सा है?
options: भारत ने पाकिस्तान के विरुद्ध **शानदार लड़ाई लड़ी**। (कर्म 'लड़ाई' और क्रिया 'लड़ी' एक ही 'लड़' धातु से बने हैं)
explanation: जब कर्म और क्रिया दोनों एक ही मूल धातु से व्युत्पन्न हों (जैसे: लड़ाई लड़ी, चाल चली), तो उसे 'सजातीय क्रिया' कहते हैं।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: कृदंत क्रिया (Participle Verb) और तद्धित में क्या अंतर है?
options: धातुओं (क्रिया मूलों) में प्रत्यय जुड़ने से बनने वाले क्रिया रूप 'कृदंत' कहलाते हैं (जैसे: लिख + ता = लिखता) ; जबकि संज्ञा/सर्वनाम/विशेषण से बनने वाले रूप 'तद्धित' कहलाते हैं
दोनों में कोई अंतर नहीं है
explanation: धातु + प्रत्यय = कृदंत (लिखकर, पढ़ता, दौड़ा); संज्ञा/सर्वनाम + प्रत्यय = तद्धित/नामधातु।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: निम्नलिखित वाक्यों में से किस वाक्य में 'अकर्मक क्रिया' प्रयुक्त हुई है?
options: 'मजदूर दिन भर से पसीना बहाकर **सो रहा है**।'
explanation: 'सो रहा है' अकर्मक क्रिया है; शेष तीनों वाक्यों में कर्म (सड़क, निबंध, खाना) उपस्थित हैं।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: तात्कालिक कृदंत क्रिया का सही उदाहरण कौन-सा है?
options: 'शेर को **देखते ही** शिकारी भाग गया।' ('देखते ही' एक क्रिया के तुरंत बाद दूसरी क्रिया का बोध कराती है)
explanation: धातु + 'ते ही' लगकर तत्क्षण दूसरी क्रिया का संपादन सूचित करने वाली क्रिया 'तात्कालिक कृदंत' कहलाती है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question:
वाक्य में प्रयुक्त रेखांकित पद का व्याकरणिक परिचय दीजिए:
'राघव ने भिखारी को **भोजन कराया**।'
explanation: 'कराया' प्रेरणार्थक क्रिया है और 'भोजन' कर्म है, अतः प्रेरणार्थक सकर्मक क्रिया है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: अकर्मक धातुओं को सकर्मक धातुओं में बदलने का सही नियम कौन-सा है?
options: हँसना (अकर्मक) -> हँसाना (सकर्मक) ; गिरना (अकर्मक) -> गिराना (सकर्मक) ; कटना (अकर्मक) -> काटना (सकर्मक)
अकर्मक को कभी सकर्मक नहीं बनाया जा सकता
explanation: अकर्मक धातुओं में आ/वा प्रत्यय जोड़कर या आदि स्वर दीर्घ करके सकर्मक क्रिया बनाई जाती है (कटना -> काटना, गिरना -> गिराना)।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: संयुक्त क्रिया के मुख्य 11 अर्थगत भेदों में से 'आरंभबोधक' और 'समाप्तिबोधक' का सही युग्म कौन-सा है?
explanation: 'धातु + लगना' = आरंभबोधक (हँसने लगा); 'धातु + चुकना' = समाप्तिबोधक (पढ़ चुका)।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question:
वाक्य को क्रिया की दृष्टि से मानक रूप में शुद्ध कीजिए:
'मेरे चाचा जी आए हैं, वह कल जाएगा।'
options: 'मेरे चाचा जी आए हैं, वे कल जाएँगे।' (आदरार्थक बहुवचन कर्ता के साथ क्रिया बहुवचन 'जाएँगे' होगी)
मेरे चाचा जी आया है, वह जाएगा।
मेरे चाचा आए, वह कल जाते।
explanation: आदरणीय व्यक्ति के लिए सर्वनाम 'वे' तथा क्रिया बहुवचन 'जाएँगे' शुद्ध मानक व्याकरण है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: क्रिया का वाक्य में क्या सर्वोच्च महत्व होता है?
options: क्रिया वाक्य का अनिवार्य केंद्र (हृदय) होती है; बिना क्रिया के कोई भी सार्थक वाक्य पूर्ण नहीं हो सकता
क्रिया केवल कविता में उपयोगी है
क्रिया के बिना भी वाक्य पूरे अर्थ दे सकते हैं
क्रिया केवल काल बताती है और कुछ नहीं
explanation: क्रिया वाक्य का अनिवार्य विधेय तत्व है, जिसके बिना वाक्य की विचार-अभिव्यक्ति असंभव है।
